newsitem.title: UK: Britain clears 4 lines of gene-modified maize.
newsitem.headline: Britain clears 4 lines of gene-modified maize.

text.p: The British government has cleared four lines of genetically modified maize for use in processed food products and as unprocessed grain in animal feed, a Ministry Of Agriculture release said.
The government accepted advice on the controversial products from an independent body of experts the Advisory Committee on Novel Foods and Processes (ACNFP).
The gene-modified maize lines are both insect-resistant and herbicide tolerant.
In its food and feed safety assessment the ACNFP concluded that the composition of grain from the GM maize did not differ significantly from conventionally bred maize.
The Food Advisory Committee recommended that there is no need for any special labelling in this case, but encouraged the provision of information on a voluntary basis.
Gene-modified products have been developed by chemical companies Ciba Geigy of Switzerland and Monsanto of the U.S.
Environmentalists and some consumer groups have opposed gene-modified products on the basis that they may cause damage to health.
